analysis:
The supplied units are CHANGELOG.md only: base text at lines 1381-1756 and head text at lines 1-232. I saw no code, configuration or executable change, so there is no changed security behavior I can trace, and I report no findings.

The head text adds an 'Autopilot daily earnings floor' entry (lines 3-9) that describes new financial and admin behavior:
- A separately funded daily earnings floor, with an independent cumulative pool.
- Admin inspection, pool-cap funding and baseline-repair endpoints.
- Persisted consent evidence and per-machine receipts, with ledger entries.
- Payments default off, and accounting archives do not yet cover the new financial tables.

The entry is relevant to A-009 (payment ledger), TB-006 (admin API) and TB-011 (App Attest and trusted-OS gating). The implementing code was not in the supplied units, so any later pass that sees it should check the following:
- Admin endpoint authorization, which falls under T-024.
- Idempotent, double-spend-safe daily settlement, in the manner of T-030.
- That floor eligibility uses authenticated trust and machine identity, not provider-reported fields.
- Overlapping session and alias handling for the 90% uptime rule, since a provider could inflate uptime.
- That erasure (T-059) covers the new tables.

The other head entries describe mitigations already in the threat-model scope: log PII removal, account erasure, the default-off soft-delete mutation gate, caller-field minimization and migration safety. They are claims in the changelog, not verified against code here.

The base text is older release notes, with no security-relevant change at those lines.
